- issue_comment created in `venue-repo`#3 ("Request: type sizes, widths, formats for figures/tables") by `venue-repo`  > Venue: NeurIPS 2026 main track, official `neurips_2026.sty` (never edited). Full record with sources: `venue.md` and `venue/neurips-2026-library.md` in this repo.
  > - Page: US Letter, ONE column. Text block 5.5 in (396 pt) wide x 9 in high. A full-width figure is `\linewidth` = 5.5 in; two side-by-side panels about 2.7 in each. Give widths as multiples of `\linewidth`, not absolute.
  > - Smallest type: the style floors are `\footnotesize` 8 pt, `\scriptsize` 7 pt, `\tiny` 6 pt. The venue states no rule for text inside figures except "neat, clean and legible", so the standard here is: figure text not below 7 pt at the size it prints, preferably 8 pt or more (body is Times 10 pt). Size each figure to its placed width and do not rescale it in LaTeX.
  > - Format: vector PDF is fine and preferred. The PDF may contain only Type 1 or embedded TrueType fonts, no Type 3: set matplotlib `pdf.fonttype=42` (and `ps.fonttype=42`). The single submission PDF must be <= 50 MB, so keep raster images modest.
  > - Height budget: the main text is 9 pages including floats. The budget is 5 figures + 2 tables (about 2 pages), so each main figure is at most about 2.3 in high at full width.
  > - Captions: below figures, table titles above tables; lower-case except the first word and proper nouns; the caption says what is shown and a take-away. Colour is allowed but figures must stay legible in black and white (differ in markers/linestyles, not colour alone).
  > - Tables: `booktabs`, no vertical rules, centred, `\small` or `\footnotesize` (>= 8 pt) at most; keep within `\linewidth`.
  > - Limits: 9 content pages include figures and tables; references, appendices and the checklist do not count and have no page limit (appendix budget 10-15 pages; Fig 6 and Tab 3 go there, as the outline says). Cut order if the text overflows: Tab 1 to the appendix first, then merge Fig 5 into Fig 4.
  > - Anonymity: no names, institution marks or identifying paths in figure or table files.
